unplain-game-config-name-reads-as-no-ent: The TS readStoredGameConfig fell back to a raw file read for a GamesConfig document whose name is not a plain segment (settingsDocs.docKeyOf refused its store key), so a hand-placed GamesConfig/dots..in.json was read (the dots..in item of read-stored-name-guards). The Rust crate reads only through the StoreHost (T-87-73), and StoreHost::open_doc refuses a name that is not a plain segment (ASCII letters, digits, dash, underscore, dot and space; no '..', no trailing dot or space, no device name; T-85-37), so such a document reads as no entry. The shell never writes one (the host refuses the same names), so the only such file is one placed by hand; engineKeyFor already refuses an appName containing '..', so no game that reaches the engine layer is affected.
settings-documents-are-the-hosts-view: The TS oracle read GamesConfig and config.json as raw files with no store root, so a document stayed in the shape the case seeded. The Rust crate reads the host's view, and opening a document runs its migration chain; the shell opens every settings document at boot, before any engine read, and the replay does the same (a boot sweep over the seeded documents) before it snapshots the tree, so a read still creates, edits and removes nothing. Every outcome of the goldens is unchanged by the migration.
registry-log-lines-and-tree-hashes-are-n: The goldens carry the TS log lines (the engine registry's 'Engine: <key> uses ...' line when a live selection is set) and a sha256 tree snapshot of the profile. The engine-config slice logs nothing (the registry is the bottle slice's), and the replay asserts the stronger property directly, byte for byte, that the profile tree is the same before and after every case; neither field is compared.
